title: Screen Time Is Over: What to Say Without Shouting | Parenting Rewind
description:
Screen time is over—but your child wants one more. This Parenting Rewind walks through a calm, specific way to end tablet time: give a clear warning, name what happens next, offer a bounded choice, acknowledge disappointment and follow through without turning the limit into a lecture.

General parenting education, not individual medical or mental-health advice. Every child and family is different.

Research basis:
• American Academy of Pediatrics / HealthyChildren.org, ‘Screen Time & Temper Tantrums: Helpful Tips for Parents’
https://www.healthychildren.org/English/family-life/Media/Pages/screen-time-and-temper-tantrums-helpful-tips-for-parents.aspx
• American Academy of Pediatrics, ‘How to Help Your Young Child Transition Away From Screens’
https://downloads.aap.org/AAP/PDF/COE_Help-your-young-child-transition-away-from-screens.pdf
• American Academy of Pediatrics / HealthyChildren.org, ‘How to Make a Family Media Plan’
https://www.healthychildren.org/English/family-life/Media/Pages/How-to-Make-a-Family-Media-Use-Plan.aspx
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
age_context: General examples for parents of children approximately ages 2–8; adapt language and choices to the individual child.
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

sources.title: Screen Time & Temper Tantrums: Helpful Tips for Parents
supports: Pause and keep the parent's voice calm during a screen-time meltdown.
Use few words rather than lecturing while the child is highly upset.
Device timers or child-set warnings may help some children transition.
Acknowledge that stopping is difficult while holding the limit.

sources.organization: American Academy of Pediatrics Center of Excellence on Social Media and Youth Mental Health
sources.title: How to Help Your Young Child Transition Away From Screens
supports: Prepare for the transition before screen use starts.
Use predictable stopping points and have an offline activity ready when practical.
Stay calm, validate feelings, and avoid returning the device because protest escalates.

sources.title: How to Make a Family Media Plan
supports: Use family-specific media rules that fit routines and values.
Turn off autoplay and notifications and preserve room for offline activities.
Adults should model the family's digital habits.

sources.title: Digital Ecosystems, Children, and Adolescents: Policy Statement
supports: Current guidance emphasizes the child, content, context, conversation, and what media crowds out rather than one universal limit.

claim_limits: Timers and advance warnings are presented as tools that may help, not guarantees.
Difficulty stopping is not described as addiction.
The episode does not claim that one daily screen-time cap fits every family.
